About the Role
We're looking for a Programmatic EHS Manager to create, train, implement, and manage Nscale 's overall Environmental, Health & Safety program for Low Voltage. You'll set the safety standards, processes, and metrics that every low-voltage project follows, and make sure they are applied consistently across sites and regions as we scale AI data center deployments.
The program covers everyone doing low-voltage work for Nscale : our full-time employees, Nscale contract employees, and the installation contractors we hire. You'll own the program for Nscale 's own workforce and manage how installation contractors' safety programs meet our standards.
Confined space entry is a major part of this role. Low-voltage work regularly takes crews into underground vaults, manholes, utility tunnels, duct banks, and other permit-required spaces, and you will make sure everyone who enters them is trained, permitted, monitored, and covered by a rescue plan.
Our sites run several safety programs at once, including the general contractor's, the site owner's, and Nscale 's own. You'll be the low-voltage team's main EHS contact with all of them. This is a program role rather than a site role, but in rare cases you will cover site safety directly when there is a gap in coverage.
What You'll Do
EHS Program Ownership

• Create, implement, and manage Nscale 's EHS program for Low Voltage, including policies, standards, procedures, and site-specific safety plans.

• Define program requirements for job hazard analyses (JHAs), pre-task planning, permits to work, and stop-work authority.

• Set standards for high-risk activities common to low-voltage work, including confined space entry, work at heights, ladders and mobile elevated work platforms (MEWPs), work near energized equipment, lockout/tagout (LOTO), core drilling and dust control, firestopping, fiber optic handling, and material handling of cable reels and trays.

• Ensure the program complies with OSHA (29 CFR 1910 and 1926, including Subpart AA for confined spaces), NFPA 70E, state requirements, and site owner and customer rules.

Training & Safety Culture

• Build and deliver the low-voltage safety training program for Nscale full-time employees, contract employees, and installation contractors.

• Confined space entry: train and verify competency for entrants, attendants, and entry supervisors before any entry, covering permits, atmospheric testing and continuous monitoring, ventilation, isolation, and communication.

• Confined space entry: ensure every entry has a written rescue plan, with rescue services that are trained, available, and able to respond in time, and audit entries in the field.

• Develop and deliver training on program standards, hazard recognition, and other high-risk work.

• Maintain training and competency records for all low-voltage personnel.

• Build a strong reporting culture where near misses and hazards are raised early and stop-work authority is used without hesitation.

Workforce & Contractor Safety Management

• Manage safety for Nscale full-time and contract employees, including onboarding, PPE, required certifications, and fitness for high-risk tasks.

• Review and approve installation contractors' safety programs, safety plans, and training records before mobilization.

• Own contractor safety prequalification and onboarding requirements, working with Procurement and project managers.

• Track contractor safety performance and drive corrective actions or escalation when expectations are not met.

Site Safety Program Integration

• Serve as the low-voltage team's EHS point of contact with the general contractor, site owner, and other trade safety programs on each site.

title: Strategy Principal, Office of the COO

Chief of Staff-level role | Walnut Insurance | Remote, Canada | Partner to the COO and CPO
The role
You'll be the operating and strategy partner to our COO and CPO. Half the job is the work a top strategy consultant does for a client: help decision, size the opportunity, build the case, pressure-test the plan, write the recommendation. The other half is what a good chief of staff does: turn that decision into execution, so momentum never depends on two people's calendars. You'll work across sales, product and partnerships as we grow in Canada and the US, in a regulated industry where banks, telcos, lenders and insurers are the buyers. And you'll do it with an AI-native toolkit that lets one person deliver what used to take a team.
About Walnut
Walnut is Canada's leading embedded insurance platform. Partners like Wealthsimple, BMO, KOHO and TELUS use us to launch insurance inside their products in 90 days, compared with nine months or more going direct to a carrier. We hold the carrier relationships, the licences and the compliance; our partners keep the customer.
Non-negotiable: you build with AI every day
You've done strategy work to a top-tier standard, in financial services. Maybe that was at a leading consultancy, in a bank or insurer's strategy or corporate development group, at a fintech or insurtech, or in a founder's office doing the same job without the title. You know how a bank, a carrier and an enterprise buyer make decisions, and how long they take. You can read a partner's P&L, a loss ratio and a take rate and tell us whether a program will make money. And you can write a board-grade recommendation on one page.
AI is how you already work, not a tool you'll pick up here. title: Category Analyst
description:
Parachute Health is transforming post-acute care as the leading digital ordering platform for medical equipment and supplies. We connect major health systems, health plans, and suppliers to help patients get the life-saving products they need at home. Since launching, we've connected 300,000+ clinicians and 3,000+ supplier locations across all 50 states and helped 15M+ patients. What started as a DME ePrescribing tool has become the order management platform of choice for home medical equipment.

Join our team and make a difference in patient care.

About the Role
As a Category Analyst (Respiratory) at Parachute, you will play a pivotal role in building and managing our catalog of respiratory products and services. You will also manage our Insurance Coverage Criteria rules engine, which helps clinicians better understand what items are covered for patients during their time of need. This role involves collaborating closely with various internal and external stakeholders to ensure that our platform offers a comprehensive range of offerings aligned with market demand and business growth strategies.
Key Responsibilities
1. Catalog Management:

• Collaborate with internal stakeholders to understand strategic areas for business expansion, such as new product categories or markets.

• Conduct in-depth analysis and research within the respiratory categories, including Oxygen, CPAP and Sleep, BiLevels, Ventilators, Nebulizers, Airway Clearance, Suction & Tracheostomy, and Testing & Monitoring. You will become a subject matter expert in product is-ness (how products exist, including their physical attributes), as well as product application (how patients, vendors, clinicians, payors, and manufacturers interact with your product categories). You will also build familiarity with market trends and Parachute's competitive landscape in your categories.

• Build and maintain the digital catalog in our Content Management System (CMS). You will analyze and organize various types and volumes of data, sourced from manufacturers and suppliers, to create product listings in our catalog. You will ensure accuracy, completeness, and usability of this catalog data.

• Continuously optimize the catalog content based on performance metrics, user feedback, and industry developments.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Product Management, Engineering, Account Management, and Customer Success, to enhance the quality and usability of the catalog.

2. Insurance Coverage Criteria Management:

• Analyze complex insurance coverage criteria requirements related to the respiratory categories (e.g., oxygen and PAP LCDs).

• Translate these criteria into a flowchart of questions and outputs to facilitate product eligibility determination (our rules engine). Bring your design to life by building, testing, and launching it on the Parachute platform.

• Attend webinars and perform periodic research to stay informed about regulatory and industry changes affecting your categories.

3. Catalog & Coverage Criteria Alignment:

Our goal is a company that runs a secure development lifecycle on every project, has its own house in order, is well on the way to ISO/IEC 27001 certification, and has an internal Security Lead who can work with you and gradually take over day-to-day ownership. This is a part-time role.

Assessment and governance

• Run the security maturity assessment yourself (for example OWASP SAMM), review our repositories, pipelines and cloud setup, and turn the findings into a prioritized roadmap.

• Write our core security policies and procedures: access control, acceptable use, secure development, incident response, vendor and AI tool usage.

• Set up and maintain the security backlog, risk register and progress metrics, and report progress to management monthly.

Company security ("secure the house")

• Configure and enforce SSO and MFA across email, Git hosting, cloud consoles, CI/CD and Passbolt.

• Review and fix access rights, and set up onboarding and offboarding checklists.

• Harden our Passbolt setup and implement a secrets manager for applications and pipelines, including migrating existing secrets out of code and CI variables.

• Implement baseline hardening for laptops, cloud accounts, backups and logging.

• Write the incident response plan and run tabletop exercises with the team.

Secure software development

• Build our standard Secure SDLC, based on OWASP ASVS and OWASP SAMM, and roll it out on real client projects.

• Configure and tune our SecOps platform: reduce false positives, set up pipeline quality gates and triage findings together with the teams.

• Add the missing scanning to our CI/CD pipelines yourself: SAST, SCA, secrets scanning, IaC and container scanning, DAST and SBOM generation.

• Run threat modeling sessions on active projects and document the results.

• Do security code reviews of high-risk changes and help developers fix vulnerabilities.

• Perform internal security testing of our applications before releases, and scope and coordinate external penetration tests.

Regulation and compliance

• Map how the EU Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), NIS2 and relevant local regulations affect us and our clients.

• Write and implement our vulnerability handling and disclosure process, including support for clients' CRA reporting obligations.

• Do the hands-on ISO/IEC 27001 preparation work: scope, risk assessment, Statement of Applicability, policies and evidence, and work with the certification body.

Client offering

• Help define security service tiers we can include in client proposals.

• Fill in client security questionnaires and build a reusable answer set.

• Join selected client meetings or calls as a senior security voice when needed.

People and knowledge

• Work side by side with our internal Security Lead so they learn by doing.

• Run short internal workshops on key topics (for example OWASP Top 10, threat modeling, secure CI/CD).

• Recommend training and certification paths for developers, Security Champions and DevOps engineers.

Must have

• 8+ years of experience in information security, with recent hands-on work in application security, DevSecOps or cloud security.

• Comfortable doing the work yourself: configuring security tools, writing pipeline configuration, reviewing code, testing applications and writing policies.

• Practical experience setting up a secure development lifecycle and integrating security tools into CI/CD pipelines.

• Good knowledge of cloud security in at least one major cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP).
